questions.prompt: What is the average-case time complexity of heapsort?
questions.rationale: Each of the n sift-down operations costs O(log n).

questions.prompt: Which of these are stable sorting algorithms?
questions.rationale: Merge and insertion sort preserve the relative order of equal keys; heapsort and quicksort do not.

questions.prompt: A binary heap is a {{1}} tree stored in an {{2}}.
questions.rationale: The complete-tree shape is what makes the implicit array layout possible.

questions.prompt: Match each operation to its worst-case cost on a binary heap.
questions.rationale: Build-heap is O(n), not O(n log n) — the bound is dominated by the many cheap shallow nodes.
